2028 Lincoln Navigator Refresh Comes From Behind the CGI Curtain, Shows All Goodies Inside and Out
25 photos
Photo: AutoYa / YouTube
The winners and losers of the latest US automotive sales reports include Mazda, Ram, Cadillac, Ford, Lincoln , Fiat, or Alfa Romeo. But which is which and who is who, plus what it does have to do with a CGI design project?
We’re into the final stretch for 2026 and so far, the automotive market has been just as convoluted as international relationships between various countries are right now. Over in America, Cadillac’s EV-heavy lineup suffered tremendously, with General Motors reporting its premium brand’s dip of 30% in the third quarter.
Concurrently, Ram jumped back into action and took over from Jeep during Q3 as the most popular brand from Stellantis, and it all has to do with the return of the Hemi V8, of course. Mazda’s ‘old cars’ like the MX-5 Miata and the Mazda3 jumped tremendously because they’re simply affordable during expensive times, while brands like Fiat or Alfa Romeo show that they don’t have any sense of direction.
Ford saw mixed results – it’s keeping the F-Series above the competition, but overall, its Q3 sales dropped while the Mustang continues to get back on the right track. Lincoln, meanwhile, dropped no less than 18% while other premium brands like Infiniti rose more than 20%, largely impacted by the phase-out of the Corsair, just as Ford took a nose-dive because it’s axing the Escape.
Soon, Lincoln is going to be left with only the Aviator, Nautilus, and the mighty Navigator. Of course, the latter remains an important halo model even though it can’t compare in terms of sales with the Nautilus. It also had the smallest gain across the past three months, up about three percent according to Ford Authority, while the Aviator is breathing down its neck with an 11% surge and the Nautilus is almost 18% up year-over-year.
No worries, as there are solutions – cue the rumor mill and the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. For example, the good folks over at the " AutoYa " info channel on YouTube have unofficially imagined the CGI looks of the mid-cycle refresh for the Lincoln Navigator to make it enticing once again, especially against fresher models like the facelifted Cadillac Escalade or the all-new Infiniti QX80, among others.
The host of the channel believes that next year the 2028 Lincoln Navigator and the long wheelbase version could get a mid-cycle refresh procedure along the same styling coordinates as the 2027 Nautilus, complete with a front-end restyle, an update to the interior with a new steering wheel and larger central display, plus additional colors.
The channel’s resident virtual artist then takes over to present the changes in an unofficial, hypothetical design project – we see the ‘new’ and ‘old’ models side-by-side both inside and outside, as always. There is also a traditional color reel, of course. So, what do you think?
